sections.overview: This large rattlesnake ranges from southern Mexico through Central America to Costa Rica.
sections.identification: Its robust body often bears dark diamond-shaped dorsal markings and a conspicuous rattle.
sections.habitat: It uses dry forests, thorn scrub, savannas and some open pine-oak landscapes, avoiding dense wet forest.
sections.diet: It eats rodents and other small vertebrates, including lizards; prey records vary among local populations.
sections.behavior: Adults are often crepuscular or nocturnal, sheltering beneath rocks, logs or in abandoned burrows by day.
sections.reproduction: This rattlesnake is viviparous; reports describe mating in winter and births during the warmer season.
sections.ecology: Older treatments grouped C. culminatus and C. tzabcan within C. simus; subsequent studies recognize them separately.
sections.conservation: Habitat conversion and deliberate killing are documented pressures, particularly where snakes enter farms and settlements.
